Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

reason noun

a cause

also the reason why, for this reason, for no reason

classical

Cic. Off. 1.101: cujus nōn possit causam probābilem reddere
Traupman 368

causa, causae f.

noun, first declension

reason, cause, ground

Hāc dē causā, for this reason; multīs dē causīs, for many reasons (Traupman 368); sine causā, for no reason (Cic.). The reason why: causa cūr or quamobrem with the subjunctive (Lewis & Short). Often Latin simply gives the reason in a clause with quod or quia.

Other words

  • ratiō, ratiōnis f. — a reason given, grounds

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. de Or. 3.207 (Lewis & Short)

    The reasoning behind a thing, the account one gives of it.

  • nihil est quod (+ subjunctive) — there is no reason to …

    phrase · also used · classical · Cic. Fam. 14.4.4: nihil est quod tē moveat; Hor. Ep. 2.1.30: nōn est quod multa loquāmur

Examples

  • nec vērō agere quicquam, cujus nōn possit causam probābilem reddere

    and to do nothing for which one cannot give a sound reasonCic. Off. 1.101

  • nōn amō tē, Sabidī, nec possum dīcere quārē

    I don’t like you, Sabidius, and I can’t say whyMart. 1.32.1

  • is ad mē rescrīpsit petīvitque ut ratiōnem dīcerem cūr tertium ac nōn tertiō scrīpsissem

    he wrote back and asked me to give my reason for writing “tertium” and not “tertiō”Gell. 10.1.2–3

  • nihil est quod tē moveat

    there is no reason for you to be upsetCic. Fam. 14.4.4

See also why, why so?, reason.
